title: Classic Mixed Vegetables, Frozen, Cooked with Butter or Margarine

content.title: About
content.content: A classic frozen vegetable mix (broccoli, carrots, cauliflower, peas) prepared with butter or margarine. The vegetables heat quickly, retain bright colour, a crisp texture and a characteristic buttery flavour.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Vegetables are flash‑frozen right after harvest, preserving most of their vitamins and minerals.
Butter gives a rich aroma, while margarine provides a more neutral taste and a longer shelf life.
The mix is a staple in school cafeterias and a convenient side dish for home cooking.
Quick thermal processing retains antioxidants such as carotenoids in carrots and vitamin C in broccoli.
Packaging is usually multi‑layered to protect against moisture and light.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: The vegetables provide vitamin B6 and folate, which support metabolism and nervous‑system function.

items.title: Source of dietary fibre
items.content: Fibre aids digestion, promotes satiety and helps maintain healthy blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Beta‑carotene, vitamin C and other antioxidants help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports bone health
items.content: Calcium and vitamin K found in broccoli and cauliflower contribute to bone strength.

items.title: Low‑calorie option
items.content: Vegetables have a low energy density, making them suitable for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Butter may trigger reactions in individuals with lactose intolerance or milk‑protein allergy.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some versions are lightly salted; people monitoring salt intake should check the label.

items.title: Trans fats in margarine
items.content: If margarine is used, it may contain trans fats, which should be limited.

items.title: Vitamin loss over time
items.content: Prolonged freezer storage can reduce certain vitamins, especially vitamin C.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the mix in the microwave or in a skillet, adding a little extra butter if needed. Serve as a side dish with meat, fish, or incorporate into quick‑prep meals. Season with herbs, garlic or soy sauce for extra flavour.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep frozen at –18 °C (0 °F) or lower. After opening, use within 3–4 months. Do not thaw and refreeze, as quality may deteriorate.
